ANC in turmoil

By: Phakamile Hlubi | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Are we witnessing the death throes of the ANC?

Unique Selling Point:
Hundreds of ANC members of the Central JHB branch have called for President Jacob Zuma's resignation. They are part of a growing number of ANC supporters calling for Zuma and the entire NEC to resign. At first they wanted to occupy Luthuli House, but because of security concerns, they ended up handing over a memorandum of their demands to the ANC, Secretary General Gwede Mantashe.

The ANC has responded with a show of force and heavy security. Why such a show of force against your own members? Why not engage their own people?



We've already seen ANC members being killed in intra-ANC violence over party posittions. After it's poor performance during local government elections, there is a real fear that the ANC will drop even further in the 2019 elections.



Summary:
Use Mondays events to look at the condition of the ANC – look historically about how Zuma was going to be the unifier and bring the ANC together and how people supported him seven years ago, and how it’s now all falling apart at the seams. Look also at how many people died in the build up to the elections showing that the ANC was already under pressure and the degree of the turmoil...

ANC NEC full of ZUMA supporters and these are the only people who can hold ZUMA to account. Make the story about prominent members of the ANC coming forward – tell the viewer more than they already know. Make it about more than just analysts telling our viewers things they already know about the fact the ANC is in turmoil...



Further information:
Carte Blanche seeks to answer the following questions:

1. What will happen now? And how does the party rebuild itself?

2. Also the level of violence that we have seen, firstly from the list party process, and the tensions which spilled over on Monday, what impact will this have not just on th eparty, but on the country?

3. If Zuma stays, what are the implications not just for the party, but for the economy of the country? Bearing in mind that we re already seeing factions playing themselves out, eg. Pravin VS. SARS.

Interview prominnt ANC leaders, Ben Turok; Ahmed Kathrada, Frank Chikane, Sipho Pityana. Also include analysts, Aubrey Matshiqi, Susan Booysen.

Press Release:


Lens on Luthuli House
This week’s #OccupyLuthuliHouse campaign brought tension to the streets flanking the ruling party headquarters. Scuffles broke out between those protesting current ANC party politics and those determined to defend it. Among demands made to the ANC by the campaign organisers are a call to immediately recall President Zuma and for the NEC to follow suite and resign. Can the ruling party withstand an onslaught from its own members? Carte Blanche asks: what do these voices of discontent mean for the ANC?
Producer: Phakamile Hlubi
Researcher: Chwayitisa Futshane

Script:


￼ANC IN TURMOIL –
LUTHULI HOUSE, JOHANNESBURG, 5 SEPTEMBER, 2016 The ANC's headquarters in Johannesburg under lockdown.
The South African Police Services brace themselves for a standoff, between a group of ANC members calling themselves #OccupyLuthuliHouse, who want President Zuma, and the entire party leadership to resign...
Whilst on the other side, Zuma loyalists are determined to defend him at the party’s headquaters.
CELLPHONE FOOTAGE HEADLINE
Flanked by members of the uMkhonto weSizwe Veterans Association, ANC Secretary General, Gwede Mantashe goes to receive a memorandum from the protestors.
But there's a problem, those defending Luthuli House, don’t want him to receive the list of grieviences. They insist that these issues must be raised at the branches.
NAT SOUND DON'T ALLOW THEM TO HAND OVER THE MEMORANDUM)
And the demonstrators feel betrayed that the party’s armed wing is being used against them.
(HOW CAN YOU BRING THE CAMOUFLAGE TO PUSH YOUR MEMBERS!)
Phakamile LINK “In the past members of the ANC have marched to Luthuli House to raise grievances. On the eve of Julius Malema’s disciplinary hearing in 2011, thousands of youth league members descended onto these streets to defend him. His subsequent expulsion resulted in the formation of the EFF. The question is what does this mean for the ANC?”

Aubrey Matshiqi, a political analyst believes the march is a reflection of a much deeper crisis..
AUBREY MATSHIQI, POLITICAL ANALYST:
“It is the problem of a former liberation movement, a party that fought for liberation that is at war with it’s own principles, with it’s own values, so if there is a conflict here, it is between the ANC in it’s current form on the one hand, and it’s values and principles on the other”
The ANC’s spokesperson Zizi Kodwa admits it was a low moment for the party.
￼
￼ZIZI KODWA, ANC SPOKESPERSON, "It was a bad image. You saw the headlines, almost all the headlines in the country, it was ANC VS ANC bite, subtitle blood bath averted. and I think that on its own it affected a lot in terms of the brand African National Congress"
Dr. Mathews Phosa, a former uMkhonto WeSizwe commander and struggle veteran believes the ANC is in danger of becoming irrelevant.
DR MATHEWS PHOSA, Former ANC Treasurer​: ​03:38:49 "​It’s for the first time in the history of the organisation that any sitting president is confronted in the streets in the manner that president Zuma has been confronted, it’s never happened before. Not with Thabo Mbeki, not Mandela, it’s never happened.”​

Since the party’s drop in support during the August polls, it’s leadership has been criss crossing the country in a bid to find solutions to its problems.
But those calling for the occupation of Luthuli House believe the answer is for President Zuma and the entire NEC to go.
RONALD LAMOLA, Former ANC Youth League Deputy President: 24:29 “He’s a leader of a cartel that is an embodiment and that has embraced all these wrong things that have affected the movement.
*Ronald Lamola served under Julius Malema as ANC Youth League Deputy President, and is himself, a former Zuma champion
(FREEZE PIC: Ronald Lamola with Julius: ­ Former ANC Youth League Deputy President 2011 – 2013)
RONALD LAMOLA, Former ANC Youth League Deputy President: 24:29 “If he is no longer there, there will be space for people to openly speak, for people to freely put their ideas forward, for people to freely shift from their factional position the organisation is going down, let’s correct it this way."
The anti­Zuma camp are convinced that the Nkandla scandal; as well as corruption charges hanging over his head; are just some of the reasons, the president should step down.

Phosa believes the president’s failure to uphold and defend the constitution on the Nkandla matter, was inconsistent with the values of the liberation movement.
DR. MATHEWS PHOSA, Former ANC Treasurer 03:41:46 “We talk about democracy, a government of the people, by the people. that’s what we talked about. We’ve got to live that. And today, don’t go an tell my child the ANC is more important than the constitution,because you are creating a problem in my mind. That’s not what I fought for”

￼The ANC’s Zizi Kodwa believes the problems facing the party are not insurmountable.
PHAKAMILE LINK: “Is it fair to say that the ANC is in crisis” (00:25:44:22)
ZIZI KODWA, ANC SPOKESPERSON, “No, no no, crisis is when you have reached a level where you can’t do anything. Challenges is when you are doing something and there is an opportunity to change the situation.

SUPER @ RONALD LAMOLA, Former ANC Youth League Dep Pres. “No it’s a crisis of unimaginable proportions.
Last week the ANC called for disciplinary action against Mineral resources minister Mosebenzi Zwane who announced that cabinet had made a decision to investigate South Africa's banking system.
This is after all the major banks decided to terminate their relationships with Oakbay investments, a company owned by the Gupta family, who are also friends of President Zuma.

SUPER @ RONALD LAMOLA, Former ANC Youth League Dep Pres: You can’t say there’s no crisis when you wake up the minister announces a judicial commission of enquiry; the presidency clarifies then there’s a threat to arrest a minister; then the there’s another clarification. Just everyday we are limping from one disaster to another”
The Gupta's have also been accused of spearheading the Hawks investigation against finance minister Pravin Gordhan.
AUBREY MATSHIQI, Political Analyst : 00:08:59 “Vulgar and crass as their displays of power maybe, the Gupta’s in my view are still the tip of the iceberg.
Matshiqi believes it will take more than Zuma’s resignation to solve the ANC’s problems...
AUBREY MATSHIQI, Political Analyst, “The broader problem we have is the extent to which since before 1994 and since 1994 different parts of the ANC and the state have been captured. And therefore these different parts of the state and the ANC that have been captured are coming into conflict with one another, and therefore competition between these different forces is manifest as conflict within the dominant party”

On the streets of Luthuli House, battle lines have been drawn.
Members of the uMkhonto WeSizwe Military Veterans Association, have vowed to keep President Zuma in power until he completes his term in 2019.
￼Their chairman, Kebby Maphatsoe has criticized those who are opposed to the current leadership.
KEBBY MAPHATSOE, CHAIRMAN uMkhonto Wesizwe Military Veterans Association
(AA450602 20 SECONDS INTO THE BITE on drive)
“It’s upon us as members of the MKMVA when there is a threat to the property and to the leadership of the African National Congress, we rise up to the occasion and go and protect the leadership and the property of the African National Congress”
DR MATHEWS PHOSA: 03:58:47 “​The ANC can only be protected by the people. not by guys who pretend to be soldiers when they have fake phantom personalities, they don't even know the smell of gun powder.”
Meanwhile officials are grappling with the challenge of uniting the organisation
PHAKAMILE : 00:35:53:09 “The divisions seem so deep though Zizi, it’s almost as if these two or three groupings can’t find each other
ZIZI KODWA, Spokesperson ANC: “The divisions may seem if you are outside of the ANC to be too deep and therefore the line is drawn. We don’t believe in that. That’s why in engagement.”
PHAKAMILE LINK: “There’s a Kenyan proverb which says when elephants fight the grass suffers. It seems clear from the divisions that there is a battle for the heart and soul of this 104 year old organisation. How this ends will have massive implications for country as a whole”

SUPER @ RONALD LAMOLA, ANC Member: 34:26 “I must be able to account to my children in future what did I do when the country and the ANC that they’ve heard of was dying. And why did they inherit a dead organization, and why are they inheriting a country in turmoil, when you were there what was your role?”

PROMO’S
PROMO 1 15 seconds
RONALD LAMOLA, FORMER ANC YOUTH LEAGUE DEP. PRES
“What did I do when the country and the ANC that they’ve heard of was dying. And why did they inherit a dead organization?”
Is factionalism destroying the oldest liberation movement in Africa?

￼PROMO 2 15 SECONDS
ZIZI KODWA, ANC Spokesperson“It was ANC VS ANC subtitle blood bath averted. and I think that on its own it affected a lot in terms of the brand African National Congress"
Is this the future of the ANC? PROMO 3 10 SECONDS
“Is #OccupyLuthuliHouse a sign of the ANC in turmoil? Can the liberation movement turn itself around before it’s too late?”
